_README: The Mechanical Balance sweep, MEASURE.md Phase 1, on the GR86. One variable
per row: bars moved alone, then the front spring moved alone.
FOUR ROWS SETTLED AND THEY GIVE MB A SHAPE. Two were photographed while the
panel still said SIMULATING and are recorded as null — see lostRows, which
is the protocol rule earning its place on the day it was written.

whatMBActuallyIs: MECHANICAL BALANCE IS THE REAR AXLE'S SHARE OF ROLL STIFFNESS, and both the
bars and the springs are in it. The direction is unambiguous across four
settled rows:
bars   30/30 -> 0.51     40/65 -> 0.55     stiffer REAR bar   -> MB UP
stiffer FRONT spring -> MB DOWN
Both say the same thing: MB rises as the rear gets relatively stiffer. It
is NOT front-over-total. Every model in MEASURE.md Phase 1 was written as
front-over-total — M1 through M5 all have the form F/(F+R) — so the whole
candidate list was the right shape upside down.
WHY THE EARLIER ONE-ROW GUESSES BOTH FAILED, now visible: bars-only fitted
the app row and springs-only fitted the default row because each was
reading the front share of ONE component of a quantity that has at least
three. The two whole-tune rows could not have distinguished them.
SOLVING THE FOUR ROWS. Write it as rear share of a weighted sum with a
per-axle constant, MB = R/(F+R) where
F = wa.arF + ws.spF + tF        R = wa.arR + ws.spR + tR
Four readings, four unknowns up to scale, so it is exactly determined and
has NO degrees of freedom left to validate with. With that caveat stated
loudly, the numbers that come out are:
wa / ws  =  about 8      one point of anti-roll bar is worth roughly
8 lb/in of spring rate
tF  =  about 0.29 x R    large per-axle constants, presumably the tires,
tR  =  about 0.41 x R    geometry and unsprung mass
The bar-to-spring ratio is the useful part and it is credible: bars run
1-65 and springs a few hundred, so 8:1 gives the two roughly comparable
authority over the full slider range, which is what a tuner would expect.
The constants being large and REAR-BIASED is the interesting part, and it
is what makes equal bars and a front-stiff spring pair still read 0.51
rather than something well under 0.5.
IT ALSO EXPLAINS THE TIRE-PRESSURE RESULT from the previous fixture: a tire
term sits inside tF and tR, so changing pressure moves them, and MB shifted
0.51 -> 0.50 with nothing else touched. Consistent, and it means pressure
must stay pinned for any future MB row.
theAppMissesItsOwnTarget: THE APP'S OWN TUNE READS MB 0.51. THE APP'S OWN TARGET BAND IS 0.55-0.65.
So a user who follows the app exactly, then opens the Verify In Game
section and checks Mechanical Balance as instructed, finds the tune outside
the band the same app told them to hit. Not marginally — 0.04 below a band
This is arguably by design: CLAUDE.md's position is that the formulas get
close and the readouts catch what the numbers cannot carry. But the gap is
systematic rather than incidental, and the app gives no indication which
way to move or by how much.
WHAT THE SWEEP SHOWS WOULD FIX IT, on this car: bars at 40/65 read 0.55,
landing exactly on the bottom of the band. That is a strongly rear-biased
pair, against the app's own nearly-equal 31.3/30.1. So the correction the
user needs is not a nudge, it is a different shape of bar setup.
Whether 0.55-0.65 is the RIGHT target is still an open, driving-only
question (case T6) and nothing here speaks to it. What is now measurable is
how to hit any target, which is exactly the split Phase 1 predicted:
solving the function is a menu job, choosing the band is a driving job.

sliderRange: THE ANTI-ROLL BAR MAXIMUM IS 65. Boston: 80 was not settable. That
confirms VMETA's arF/arR hi of 65 in index.html:549-550 against the game
for the first time, and it is a piece of case R3 answered in passing.
It also reshapes the same-ratio pair, which was written as 20/40 against
40/80. 40/80 is unreachable. The pair that fits inside the range and holds
the same 1:2 ratio is 20/40 against 32.5/65 — and the ARB step is 0.1, so
notes: Lateral G sat at 1.26 and 1.42 on every row of this sweep, unmoved by a bar pair going from 30/30 to 40/65 and by the front spring moving from 328 to 608. Combined with the pressure row, that is now three separate tune changes that do not move lateral G. Case S5 asks whether lateral G responds to the tune at all; the answer is looking like no, which would mean the panel cannot see grip-side tuning and those constants stay lap-times-only. Braking did move with the springs — 68.4 ft at the soft front spring against 66.6 at the stiff one — so the panel is not blind to the suspension, just to whatever lateral G is measuring.
